cells.tense: You are here holding a beginning that hasn't landed anywhere yet, and still carrying what you already started.
cells.act: carry on with the version you chose through another week of doubt
cells.ask: Take the one you already chose and keep it going — through the doubt if it comes, and through the flat days too. If a week is too tight a frame, let it simply run.
cells.core:
There's a start in you that hasn't found its shape yet, and there's also the load you're already carrying. Neither has to be right yet. What you can do is stay with the version you picked, another stretch, through the doubt or the flat days, and that staying is the thing.

So choose to keep it going a while longer. The doubt may not leave; it doesn't have to. You've borne things through worse without a sign that any of it was working, and this is the same muscles, the same quiet way with weight. What you get for it is a start that starts to look like yours, held long enough to look back at. The choice only counts while it's still hard enough to be a choice, and it is.
cells.sheetLine: Keep the one you chose going another stretch.
cells.verb: Lighting something before you can see where it's headed.
cells.place: Where the weight is carried and the form holds.

cells.tense: You are bracing for a starting that hasn't happened yet, and forcing a shape onto something that hasn't taken one.
cells.act: lay every piece of it out where you can see all of it at once
cells.ask: Put everything you're carrying on one page — all of it, nothing sorted into better or worse — and look at the whole picture without changing a thing.
cells.core:
You're trying to hold a shape that hasn't formed, and it's costing more than the hauling. Everything is at once — total presence, total readiness — and that much light makes it hard to see what's actually there. You're carrying past what's here, and the weight in your hands has stopped matching it.

So see the whole of it at once. Every piece out on one page, nothing sorted into better and worse, nothing fixed while you look. When nothing's hidden, including the parts you'd rather not show yourself, the force goes out of it. The bracing eases. What you're really holding becomes visible then, and it's a smaller, steadier thing than the one you were hauling around.
cells.sheetLine: Lay the whole of it out before you carry it further.
cells.verb: Lighting something before you can see where it's headed.
cells.place: Where the weight is carried and the form holds.

cells.tense: Something in you began and stays at the door, and you are still standing where it started.
cells.act: name every feeling in it on one page, none of them crossed out
cells.ask: Write the feeling out — every colour of it, nothing edited out — and only after the page is full, decide about the next step.
cells.core:
A thing began in you and didn't get to land. You're still holding the start back the way you did the day it began, and sitting with it unfelt is where your energy goes. The pause is real; it isn't laziness, or a lack of wanting.

So write the feeling out before you take another step. Not to move on right away and not to decide — just to take the full measure, what's yours and what's sat unnamed. Once every colour of it is on the page, the next thing gets somewhere to go, and the waiting stops being the place you spend your days. Knowing it completely is what lets it begin to move.
cells.sheetLine: Holding it unfelt still costs you the other side of it.
cells.verb: Lighting something before you can see where it's headed.
cells.place: Where the weight is carried and the form holds.

cells.tense: You keep something going and carry it alone, and you speak about it as if it runs by itself.
cells.act: use the finished thing for an hour instead of improving it
cells.ask: Use what you finished as it stands — no edits, no upgrades — and postpone the improvements until tomorrow.
cells.core:
You are the one keeping the start alive. It runs because you keep turning back to it, and by your telling it doesn't depend on anyone, least of all you. The hours of upkeep go unmentioned, mostly by you, and the thing you keep looks like something you merely found.

Let what you made be finished for an hour. Use it as it stands — one meal, one pass, one small test — and hold off on the polishing. Satisfaction gets to land there. This is the older way you started things, before the upkeep quietly became a second job: you made a thing, and it was enough as it was. That way is still yours, and nobody needs to know it was you who kept it alive.
cells.sheetLine: What you keep alive is your doing, and it can be enough as it stands.
cells.verb: Lighting something before you can see where it's headed.
cells.place: Where the weight is carried and the form holds.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person is carrying a live bright want, since the record only names a start that hasn't found its shape yet; a reader could say they feel no fire at all right now and are simply holding the days together. The asks survive that: growing an existing thing in place, watching a beginning finish, putting down what's kept going unheeded, and eating a finished meal all work without any felt spark. The sentences that serve the writer more than the person are the ones about sparks, ignition, and stars — the Activation prose — so they come down to plain carrying and ordinary beginnings.
